audit.why: Trundle taking levels 1-5 and the lane flattening to skill from 6 matches the kits and the 56.59% over 334 games: Mundo has no dash and no hard CC to break a Frozen Domain trade, and his resistances stay low while he stacks health — which is exactly what Subjugate takes a percent of.

audit.whatIsWrong: The late spike says Maximum Dosage 'fully heals Mundo through a prolonged skirmish' without stating the one thing that decides it — it is a flat 120s cooldown and Grievous Wounds has to already be on him when he presses it, not applied afterwards.
audit.why: Riot's Maximum Dosage text: 'instantly healing a percent of his missing Health. He then gains Move Speed and regenerates a portion of his maximum Health over a long duration.' Cooldown 120 at every rank. The instant portion is a burst heal, so anti-heal applied after the cast has already missed most of it.
audit.corrected: Spike and the dos now carry the 120s number and the 'Grievous Wounds first, then commit' order.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four errors and one large omission. (a) mid says 'Chomp's AS debuff slows his own healing rate by reducing his auto frequency' — Chomp saps Attack Damage, not attack speed, and none of Mundo's healing is auto-driven. (b) mid says 'Bait his cleaver (E is on a long cooldown early)' — the cleaver is Infected Bonesaw on Q at a 4-second cooldown; E is Blunt Force Trauma at 9s. You cannot bait a 4-second spell. (c) early calls the cleaver 'short range' — it is 975, longer than anything Trundle has. (d) The omission: Heart Zapper only heals him if its burst hits an enemy.
audit.why: Riot Data Dragon. Infected Bonesaw: 4s, 975 range, 'dealing damage to the first enemy hit based on their current health' — so the first minion in the path eats it, which is the actual counter. Heart Zapper: 17/16.5/16/15.5/15, 325 range, 'stores a portion of damage he takes. At the end of the duration or on Recast, Dr. Mundo deals a burst of damage to nearby enemies. If the burst hit an enemy, he heals a percentage of the stored damage' — leave the 325 radius before it pops and the entire heal is denied. Goes Where He Pleases: he 'resists the first Immobilizing effect... dropping a chemical cannister nearby. Dr. Mundo can pick it up by walking over it, restoring Health and reducing this Ability's Cooldown' — Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain and can wall him off that pickup.
audit.corrected: AD sap corrected, the Q/E mix-up fixed, the 975-range minion-block counter written in, the Heart Zapper burst-must-hit rule stated as the core sequencing, and the cannister denial added to the late block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this entry as having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and that was accurate — not a single duration appeared in either layer.
audit.why: Heart Zapper 17s, Infected Bonesaw 4s, Blunt Force Trauma 9s, Maximum Dosage 120s. The 17s W is the one that carries a real 'wait for X before you Y': step out of the 325 radius, let the burst fizzle, then commit.
audit.corrected: 17s / 4s / 120s and the step-out-before-it-pops sequence now appear in the cooldown block, the dos, the report, mid and the late spike.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain spike + reset. Duel when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Dr. Mundo Infected Bonesaw: Throws a cleaver that slows and deals %current-HP magic damage; refunds HP. Dodge or sidestep it.

edits.before: At level 1, walk up and Q Chomp on the first auto trade — the AD steal immediately weakens his ability to trade back and King's Tribute heals you off every minion wave that dies nearby. Mundo has no meaningful kill threat pre-6; his Q cleaver does percent-HP damage but has a short range and a travel time, so step to the side of his throw arc and deny him the poke. At level 2, drop Frozen Domain under your feet the moment he steps up and extend every trade for at least three autos — his early resistances are so low that Chomp's bonus damage and the ice zone's attack speed bonus win any exchange that lasts more than two seconds.
edits.after: At level 1, walk up and Q Chomp on the first auto trade — the AD sap immediately weakens his ability to trade back and King's Tribute heals you off every minion wave that dies nearby. Mundo has no meaningful kill threat pre-6; Infected Bonesaw reaches 975 and stops on the first enemy it touches, so keep a minion between you and the throw and the poke never reaches you at all. At level 2, drop Frozen Domain under your feet the moment he steps up and extend every trade for at least three autos — his early resistances are so low that Chomp's bonus damage and the ice zone's attack speed bonus win any exchange that lasts more than two seconds.

edits.before: From levels 4 onward he starts building HP and a little armor, but his resistances are still low enough that Subjugate at 6 is effectively a death sentence. Bait his cleaver (E is on a long cooldown early) by walking toward him, let it miss or tank one hit, then Pillar of Ice behind him to cut off his retreat and all-in under Frozen Domain — he has no dash or hard CC to interrupt your W zone. Do not let the fight go so long that his passive regen stacks up meaningfully; Chomp's AS debuff slows his own healing rate by reducing his auto frequency, so weave Chomps throughout the trade. At 6 cast Subjugate immediately when you open the all-in — drain the first half of his Armor and MR, then fight inside Frozen Domain until you choose whether to cast the second Subjugate hit to take the rest.
edits.after: From levels 4 onward he starts building HP and a little armor, but his resistances are still low enough that Subjugate at 6 is effectively a death sentence. Infected Bonesaw is back every 4 seconds, so there is nothing to bait — body-block it with a minion instead, then Pillar of Ice behind him to cut off his retreat and all-in under Frozen Domain; he has no dash and no hard CC to interrupt your W zone. The sequencing that actually matters is Heart Zapper: it banks the damage you deal for 17 seconds and only heals him if the burst hits something, so when it lights up, step outside the 325 radius, let it pop on nothing, then walk back in. At 6 cast Subjugate the instant you open — the steal doubles over 4 seconds, so opening with it is worth about twice closing with it.

edits.before: Once Mundo hits two completed tank items and Maximum Dosage, a sustained 1v1 where he activates R becomes unwinnable — he heals too much HP for your individual damage to overcome before Subjugate's drain expires. Shift your gameplan to team fights: open with Subjugate on him when your team is nearby so his stripped resistances make him a focus target for the entire squad, not just you. Use Pillar of Ice to separate him from his team or prevent his retreat when he tries to heal up in fog. Your window to close out the game cleanly is before his second tank item completes — if you are ahead, force objectives and end; if even, play for the Subjugate-into-team-burst pattern rather than the solo duel.
edits.after: Once Mundo hits two completed tank items and Maximum Dosage, a sustained 1v1 where he activates R becomes unwinnable — he heals too much HP for your individual damage to overcome before Subjugate's drain expires. Shift your gameplan to team fights: open with Subjugate on him when your team is nearby so his stripped resistances make him a focus target for the entire squad, not just you. Pillar of Ice separates him from his team, and it also walls him off the chemical cannister his passive drops when your team's first hard CC lands — that pickup heals him and shortens the cooldown. Your window to close the game cleanly is before his second tank item; if you are ahead, force objectives and end.

edits.before: Iceborn Gauntlet Chomp spam keeps the AD steal and slow active through every trade, denying his passive regen from outpacing your damage before he reaches his tank item breakpoints.
edits.after: Iceborn Gauntlet Chomp spam keeps the AD sap and slow active through every trade, and stepping out of Heart Zapper's 325 radius denies the heal before he reaches his tank breakpoints.

notes: The packet defect 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' was accurate — neither layer contained a single number. The fix that answers it is Heart Zapper: Riot's text says he heals only 'if the burst hit an enemy', so stepping outside the 325 radius before it pops denies the whole heal. That is now the core sequencing line in mid, the cooldown block, the dos and the report. Also corrected: 'Chomp's AS debuff slows his own healing rate' (Chomp saps AD, and none of Mundo's healing is auto-driven), 'Bait his cleaver (E is on a long cooldown early)' (the cleaver is Q at 4s; E is Blunt Force Trauma at 9s), and 'short range' for a 975-range throw — the real counter is that it stops on the first enemy hit, so a minion eats it. Newly added: Pillar of Ice can wall Mundo off the chemical cannister his passive drops, which otherwise heals him and refunds the passive's cooldown. packets/trundle.json gives 56.59 (334 games) but MC_WR_TABLES.trundle.drmundo is 47.41 — a 9.2-point gap, the largest in the slice, and the diff/diffRating pair here ('HARD' at 7/10 against a 56.59% win rate) reads off as well.
